source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which feature suggests a tumor is malignant rather than benign?
questions.rationale: Malignant tumors grow rapidly, infiltrate tissues, are not encapsulated and have poorly differentiated cells.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Benign vs. malignant (PDF p. 14)
questions.quote: Infiltrates surrounding tissues

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which test gives the definitive diagnosis of cancer?
questions.rationale: Biopsy, with tissue examination, is the most accurate test for cancer.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Cancer detection (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: Biopsy- the most accurate test for cancer

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pain is usually which kind of sign in cancer?
questions.rationale: Cancer is initially painless (e.g., nontender breast mass, painless hematuria); pain is a late sign.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Pathophysiology (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Pain is a late sign of cancer

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A patient with bone metastasis has fatigue, constipation, polyuria and weak reflexes. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Bone metastasis releases calcium: fatigue, anorexia, constipation, polyuria, weakness and diminished DTRs.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Hypercalcemia (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: Signs and symptoms include fatigue, anorexia, nausea and vomiting, constipation, polyuria, severe muscle weakness, diminished deep tendon reflexes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When preparing chemotherapy, the nurse should:
options: Wear gloves, mask and back-closing gown
Prepare it in the open ward
questions.rationale: Safe handling: protective gloves, mask and back-closing gown, ideally a laminar flow hood, and hazardous waste disposal.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Safe handling of chemotherapy (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: Wear mask, gloves and back closing gown.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A patient on chemotherapy has stomatitis. Which mouth care is best?
questions.rationale: Stomatitis: frequent saline rinses and soft care; avoid alcohol mouthwash, citrus and trauma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Chemotherapy side effects (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Good oral care for stomatitis. Use warm saline rinse.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A patient's platelet count is low after chemotherapy. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Thrombocytopenia: electric razor, soft brush, no flossing, avoid aspirin/NSAIDs and straining.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Thrombocytopenia (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Male clients: use electric razor

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A mother visiting her neutropenic son on chemotherapy brings a bouquet of roses and a basket of mangoes. What should the nurse do?
options: Not allow them in the room
questions.rationale: Neutropenic precautions: no fresh flowers, fresh fruit or raw foods; limit visitors.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Neutropenia (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: No fresh fruits/ fresh flowers in the patient's unit

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: To prevent hemorrhagic cystitis from cyclophosphamide, the patient should:
questions.rationale: Cyclophosphamide can cause hemorrhagic cystitis; high fluid intake dilutes irritating metabolites.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Hemorrhagic cystitis (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Increase fluid intake to 2,500 mls/day

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before each dose of doxorubicin, the nurse should check the:
questions.rationale: Doxorubicin and daunorubicin are cardiotoxic; monitor ECG and cardiac function.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Chemotherapy side effects (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Check ECG changes if the patient receives Daunorubicin, Doxorubicin. These drugs are cardiotoxic.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug is the antidote given with high-dose methotrexate?
questions.rationale: Leucovorin (folinic acid) rescues normal cells from methotrexate toxicity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Chemotherapy side effects (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: The antidote for methotrexate is Leucovorin.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which chemotherapy drug requires close monitoring of urine output for nephrotoxicity?
questions.rationale: Cisplatin is nephrotoxic; bleomycin causes pulmonary toxicity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Chemotherapy side effects (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Cisplatin is nephrotoxic. Monitor intake and output

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A patient asks if he will be radioactive after external beam radiation. The nurse answers:
questions.rationale: External radiation leaves no residual radioactivity; activities resume right after.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 External radiation therapy (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Inform patient that there is no- residual radioactivity.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Skin over an external radiation field is red and dry. The nurse teaches the patient to:
options: Wash with plain water and pat dry
questions.rationale: Keep the area dry, wash with water only, pat dry; avoid ointments, heat, sun and removing markings.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Skin reactions (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Wash area with water, no soap; pat dry (do not rub).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A patient with a cervical radiation implant is in bed. Which is correct care?
questions.rationale: Complete bed rest, urinary catheter and low-residue diet prevent dislodgement; pregnant staff are not assigned.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Internal radiation (PDF p. 22)
questions.quote: Complete bed rest. - to prevent dislodgement of the radioisotope

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The nurse finds a cervical implant lying in the bed. The best initial action is to:
questions.rationale: Use long-handled forceps to place it in the lead container kept in the room; never touch it or reinsert it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Internal radiation (PDF p. 22)
questions.quote: use long forceps to pick up the dislodged radioisotope

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which three principles protect the nurse caring for a patient with a radiation implant?
questions.rationale: Limit time, keep distance when not giving care, and use shielding.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Radiation protection (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: Principles of Radiation Protection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a modified radical mastectomy, the best position is:
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's aids lung expansion; elevating the affected arm promotes drainage and prevents lymphedema.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Postop breast surgery (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: semi-Fowler's position with arm abducted and elevated on pillows

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After mastectomy, which arm care prevents lymphedema?
options: No BP or needles on that arm
questions.rationale: Arm precautions: no BP, injections or blood draws on the affected side; avoid any trauma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Postop breast surgery (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: No BP taking or puncturing of the arm on affected site.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After emptying a Hemovac drain, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Compressing the Hemovac before closing restores negative pressure (suction).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Postop breast surgery (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: compress it before covering it to reestablish suction/negative pressure

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which lab results suggest tumor lysis syndrome after chemotherapy?
options: High K, high uric acid, low Ca
questions.rationale: TLS: hyperkalemia, hyperuricemia, hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia, risking renal failure.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Tumor lysis syndrome (PDF p. 27)
questions.quote: Hyperkalemia Hyperuricemia Hyperphosphatemia Hypocalcemia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A lung cancer patient has facial swelling, distended neck veins and dyspnea. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: SVC obstruction reduces venous return: facial and arm swelling, JVD, dyspnea and orthopnea.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Superior vena cava syndrome (PDF p. 27)
questions.quote: Facial swelling J VD (jugular vein distention)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A patient with metastatic cancer reports new back pain. Why is this urgent?
options: It may signal spinal cord compression
It is from bed rest only
questions.rationale: Back pain usually precedes neurologic deficits in spinal cord compression; early steroids and radiation prevent paralysis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 2 Spinal cord compression (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: It causes backpain, usually before neurological deficits occurs.
